data.text:
'CORRUPTION AT ITS WORST'

Two Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) officials were relieved for allegedly receiving kickbacks from overpriced fire extinguishers.

According to Mav Gonzales’ Monday report on “24 Oras,” the BFP officials allegedly collected P30 million from selling fire extinguishers to just one building.

The two BFP officials, one from BFP-Quezon City and the other BFP-National Capital Region, were placed under administrative relief to avoid interfering with the ongoing investigation.

Those applying for BFP permits were allegedly pressured to buy fire extinguishers at double or triple the price, or they would face delays or denial of business and building permits.

data.text:
PROBE ON ALLEGED ANOMALIES IN BFP

Iniimbestigahan ng Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) ang ilang indibidwal kaugnay ng umano’y isyu ng korupsyon sa Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), ayon kay DILG Sec. Jonvic Remulla.

“Ang pormal na iniimbestigahan namin is the former Bids and Awards Committee last year and the several personnel from the [Quezon City] Fire Department and from the NCPRO, and the general leadership of the BFP,” saad ni Remulla.

Sinabi rin ng kalihim na nagtalaga sila ng special task force at bumili ng 14,000 body cameras na ikakabit sa mga fire inspector.

“So, may script na sila. May sasabihin na ‘nandito po kami para sa fire inspection.’ [...] Lahat ho ‘to naka-body camera… Kung sisitahin nila ‘yung fire extinguisher, dapat sitahin nila properly. Sabihin nila kung ano ang defect pero hindi sila pwedeng mag-recommend kung ano ang bibilhin na fire extinguisher,” aniya.
